A detail plot of [2126,2253] instead showed a sustained positive trend (slope ≈+0.023/pt, violating reference slope |<0.0023|) and elevated roughness, suggesting a trend anomaly spanning the full interval; however, this appeared to be an artifact of windowing that captured only part of a broader deviation. A Compare against the best-matching reference (index 0, shape distance 0.265, reliability 0.98) clarified that the true anomaly is a shapelet: the rising flank of the second peak in [1915,2463], specifically [2189,2257], exhibits dense high-frequency ripples (~10–15 pt period, ~0.3–0.5 z-units) absent in references and other peaks, while preserving overall cycle timing/amplitude—confirming a localized morphological deviation, not a point or trend anomaly. The earlier point candidate [2187,2195] overlaps the shapelet’s onset and is subsumed by it; the shapelet was marked with confidence 0.87. No unresolved uncertainty remains about the anomaly type or interval, though confidence is moderate due to morphological subtlety.
